column2: The rain had not let up since morning, and the windows of the reading room were grey with it.
Sarah crossed to the window, moving slowly, and stood there a while without saying anything at all.
You have been standing there, quite still, for a quarter of an hour, she said.
I have been thinking, on and off, since breakfast, Thomas replied, without turning from the desk.
You have been avoiding the letter.
He set down his pen at last.
It is not the letter I am avoiding, he said. "It is the answer to it."
The clock in the hall struck four, and neither of them moved.
Then read it to me, said Sarah, "and we will be afraid of it together."
Thomas laughed, which surprised them both.
That is the first sensible thing, in this house, that anyone has said today.
He took the envelope from the drawer, and turned it over once, and did not open it.
Outside, the rain kept on as it had all morning, indifferent to the pair of them.
